title: Streaming and Real-time AI Responses
why: Until now our endpoints returned the answer whole: the user stared at an empty screen for 2–8 seconds. Every modern AI chat shows the answer as it's being written. Today we get the answer from Gemini in pieces, send it to the client right away with Server-Sent Events, and add cancellation — so we don't pay for Gemini's tokens after the user has left. Without this skill an AI chat doesn't look like a product.
outcomes: You'll explain what streaming changes (TTFT) and what it doesn't (the total time)
You'll get the answer piece by piece with `GetStreamingResponseAsync` and `await foreach`, and measure when each piece arrives
You'll write an SSE endpoint with `TypedResults.ServerSentEvents` and an async iterator (`yield return`), and check it with `curl -N`
You'll pass a `CancellationToken` in three places so that the Gemini request stops when the client leaves

review.q: Does streaming make the answer faster? What actually changes?
review.a: The total time is almost the same · what changes is the TTFT — the time to the first word (seconds → milliseconds) · the user starts reading right away, no more empty screen

review.q: What does `GetStreamingResponseAsync` return and how do we read it?
review.a: An `IAsyncEnumerable<ChatResponseUpdate>` — a stream of pieces · `await foreach` — waits for the next piece · `update.Text` — a chunk of text; the same messages/options, tools work too

review.q: In `/stream-timing` Gemini was streaming, but Swagger showed everything at once. Why? How did we fix it?
review.a: We collected the pieces in a list and returned it at the end — the stream stopped in the Controller · an async iterator (`yield return`) + `TypedResults.ServerSentEvents` — each piece goes to the client right away

review.q: What is SSE and why is it enough for an AI chat (instead of WebSocket/SignalR)?
review.a: An HTTP response with `text/event-stream` that stays open; `data: …` + an empty line · an AI answer is one-way (server → client) · WebSocket/SignalR are for two-way communication

review.q: Where did we pass the `CancellationToken`, and why?
review.a: ① the action parameter (RequestAborted) ② `[EnumeratorCancellation]` in the iterator ③ to `GetStreamingResponseAsync` · the client left → the Gemini request stops → no more tokens are spent

quiz.q: Gemini's answer takes 6 seconds. What changes with streaming?
options: The first word appears in under ~a second; the total time stays almost the same
quiz.explain: Streaming reduces the TTFT — Gemini writes at the same speed.
An asynchronous stream of pieces — read with await foreach.

options: Yes — UseFunctionInvocation runs the loop with streaming too
quiz.explain: The same options, the same loop; the text arrives after the tool's result.

quiz.q: In `/stream-timing` Swagger showed all the pieces at once. Why?
options: We collected the pieces in a list and returned `Ok(chunks)` at the end
quiz.explain: The ms values show Gemini was streaming — the stream stopped in the Controller.

quiz.q: Why is SSE enough for an AI chat, with SignalR not required?
options: An AI answer is one-way (server → client); SSE is plain HTTP, with no extra library
quiz.explain: For two-way communication (a game, a chat between people) — WebSocket/SignalR.

quiz.q: What does `yield return update.Text` do in an async iterator?
options: Adds the text to a list
Returns the piece to the caller right away — and ServerSentEvents sends it to the client
Sends a new request to Gemini
quiz.explain: No list needed — the stream doesn't break between Gemini and the client.

quiz.q: Who fills in the action's `CancellationToken` parameter?
options: ASP.NET Core — HttpContext.RequestAborted, cancelled when the client leaves
quiz.explain: Exactly as in the API course's async endpoints.

quiz.q: What happens if we don't pass the token to `GetStreamingResponseAsync`?
options: After the client leaves, the request to Gemini may go on to the end — we pay for tokens for nothing
Nothing — the token is optional and always unnecessary
quiz.explain: Pass the token to every async call — AI requests are long and cost money.
